title: Let only genuine requests through to the network

blocks.text: An acquirer forwards every terminal request to its network. On the morning of the security test, the testers report three findings: a purchase whose amount they changed on the way was approved, a purchase they sent with no MAC was approved, and every PIN purchase from a new terminal comes back from the network as `55`, incorrect PIN, though the cardholders typed the right one.
`TerminalGate` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TerminalGate.java` is the first participant of the chain. `prepare` already decides what happens; finish the two methods it calls, marked `TODO`:

items: `macVerifies`: whether this request really comes from the terminal it names;
`forNetwork`: what the network receives in place of the terminal's request.

blocks.text: `QueryHost` comes later in the chain and sends whatever `forNetwork` returned. `macInput`, `hsm()` and `keys()` are given. About twelve lines in total.

The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with a real `QueryHost` and QMUX in the test's own JVM, with a real software security module and key file. Two terminals and the network hold their own copies of the keys.

cases.says: a purchase signed by a known terminal reaches the network and comes back approved
a request changed after the terminal signed it is refused with 63 and never reaches the network
a request with no MAC at all is refused like a forged one
a terminal with no key on file is answered 63 rather than left without an answer
what the network receives carries no MAC under the terminal's key
a PIN purchase reaches the network with the PIN under the key the network shares, so the network can check it
a PIN purchase whose PIN can't be translated is refused with 96 and never reaches the network, not sent on without its PIN

origin.section: 7.3 A PIN Block Is Safe Only While Its Key and the LMK Stay Apart

concepts: A request's MAC is verified under the key of the terminal it names, before any participant acts on it; a missing MAC or an unknown terminal fails like a wrong MAC, and a participant that sends in prepare acts before a later abort.

A PIN block is translated from the TPK of the terminal in field 41 to the network's key, on a copy for the network without the terminal's MAC; a block that can't be translated is refused, never sent on without it.
